📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia co-founder and now former CEO Jensen Huang has never been as prone to controversy as AI leaders like OpenAI’s Sam Altman or SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk. But the 63-year-old industry kingpin recently admitted that he cheated on his wife of 40 years in affairs that could have ramifications beyond Huang’s personal life and U.S. national security.

According to recent reports, U.S. officials believe that one of Huang’s likely romantic interests, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy who has been feeding information back to Beijing. (Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen, is of no relation to Jensen Huang.).

Industry observers note that megaspeed is a Singapore-based AI infrastructure company that reportedly purchased $4.8 billion worth of Nvidia chips over the last two years. The U.S. and Singapore have both previously investigated Megaspeed over suspicions that the firm was illegally sharing chips with China. The Justice Department has since taken over the federal investigation into the company, The New York Times has reported.

The story took a sudden turn on Wednesday. Citing five people who worked at Nvidia, the Times reported that Huang also had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of healthcare, who reports directly to him. Nvidia, Huang and Powell have not confirmed the report. Reached by a Times reporter, Huang reportedly mentioned, “I don’t think you should be talking to me directly,” before hanging up.

Industry observers note that by early Thursday morning, Huang was no longer CEO of the company he co-founded 33 years ago. Then, Thursday afternoon, Reuters dropped another bombshell, publishing a report alleging that Huang had yet another extramarital affair with another unnamed Nvidia employee.

According to recent reports, the U.S. and China are embroiled in a fierce technological arms race to build the most advanced AI infrastructure, which could shape each country’s economic future, military prowess, and capacity for innovation. Nvidia is valuable in this competition as one of the world’s largest makers of AI chips, which are essential for accelerating AI development. But as an American manufacturer, Nvidia faces government restrictions on the sale of its most powerful chips to Chinese entities.

As the controversy unfolds, we are organizing the most relevant events into a reverse-chronological timeline to keep you up to date.

Recent findings suggest that nvidia reported its quarterly earnings on Tuesday, which beat Wall Street expectations with $115.8 billion in revenue, up 103% year-over-year. Despite the unknowns the company faces without Huang involved, interim CEO Colette Kress remarked that full-year revenue is also on track to exceed expectations. The company also prepares to raise its outlook for the 2028 fiscal year, indicating confidence that this unexpected leadership change won’t get in the way of its trajectory.

Industry observers note that “We have the best technologists on the planet with a world-class multi-year roadmap,” Kress stated. “From a business perspective, it’s business as usual. We’ve engaged with our customers, we’ve engaged with our suppliers, our partners. They’re all 100% behind us.”.

It has been revealed that nvidia chairman Harvey C. Jones affirmed that the company is not considering reinstating Huang. Kress also noted that Nvidia will no longer sell its H200 chips in China, ending the company’s participation in a controversial loophole in the U.S. ban on the sale of advanced chips to the country.

Jensen Huang posted his first public statement since he admitted to having an extramarital affair more than a week earlier.

According to recent reports, “Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company. If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO,” he wrote.

Many of Huang’s colleagues in the tech industry, including Elon Musk, Anduril founder Palmer Luckey, and Y Combinator President and CEO Garry Tan, have called for his return.

Over the past week, I’ve been overwhelmed by the love and support of friends, industry colleagues, and people I've never met. Thank you to everyone who has shown kindness to my family and me. It means the world to me.I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an….

More reports continue to roll out that illustrate the shock and severity of Huang’s resignation from Nvidia.

Bloomberg reported that Huang looked “broken and shattered, his legendary energy depleted” by the time he surrendered his role on Wednesday night, uttering phrases like “whatever” and “I don’t care.”.

Separately, The Wall Street Journal reported that Huang had been critical of his CFO and current interim CEO, Colette Kress. Huang is said to have described Kress as “a deer in the headlights” during a presentation this summer, and he had described Kress as someone who could not help him steer strategy or decision-making.

In a scathing letter sent to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, Representative Richard Neal (D-MA) and Senator Ron Wyden (D-OR) noted they will investigate how the Trump administration handled Nvidia’s chip sales to China, especially after Trump was briefed about Huang’s relationship with a purported Chinese spy.

It has been revealed that “Although [Lutnick] and President Trump were reportedly briefed on this intelligence, the Administration did not appear to acknowledge this evident national security threat. On the contrary: despite reportedly learning of Mr. Huang’s compromising relationship last fall, President Trump granted Nvidia permission to sell its advanced H200 AI chips to China in December 2025 in exchange for a cut of the export sales,” the letter states.

That same evening, Senator Tim Scott (R-SC) requested that Huang and Lutnick both testify before the Senate Banking Committee.

“The American people deserve answers,” Scott wrote on X.

After Huang was already ousted from Nvidia, we continued to learn more incriminating claims about the former CEO. According to Reuters, Huang had a third affair with an additional, unnamed employee of Nvidia.

Nvidia noted its board had accepted Huang’s resignation on Wednesday. The firm’s current CFO, Colette Kress, will take over as interim CEO while still fulfilling her CFO duties. Nvidia is expected to conduct a larger search to determine a permanent successor to Huang.

Sources indicate that harvey C. Jones, a managing partner of Square Wave Ventures and former CEO of Synopsys, was appointed as the company’s first-ever chair of the board of directors. Jones has been on Nvidia’s board since 1993.

Later in the day, Huang confirmed that he would testify in Congress at some point before Thanksgiving, which falls on November 26.

It has been revealed that “Jensen and I have been very at odds as some of you already know on export controls, but Nvidia is a very vital organization to the United States of America,” House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast mentioned to reporters. “I don’t want to see anything hurt in Nvidia, but he has some very serious questions to answer.”.

The testimony is expected to take place behind closed doors, but Mast believes the briefing will be recorded and transcribed.

Recent findings suggest that after reports of a second extramarital affair, Nvidia’s board reportedly plans to meet to discuss Huang’s future at the company, per The Wall Street Journal. Stock fell about 8% in after-hours trading on Wednesday and is down 11% in the past five days.

Huang famously delegates very little and has about 60 direct reports, he has stated. The manufacturer has not had an obvious successor or a succession proposal.

The Newly introduced York Times reported that Jensen Huang also had an affair with Nvidia vice president of healthcare Kimberly Powell, who reports directly to the CEO.

According to the report, Huang and Powell were captured on film “being affectionate” at a hotel during a conference earlier this year.

Industry observers note that huang has not responded to a request from three Republican congressmen to appear for a closed-door briefing for questioning about his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. House China Committee Chairman John Moolenaar said Wednesday on Fox Business that if Huang doesn’t agree to the briefing, he’ll likely be subpoenaed.

The Nvidia CEO pulled out of upcoming speaking engagements at the ElevenLabs Summit and Anthropic CEO Forum.

It has been revealed that alice Huang and her family reportedly built a network of companies in China and Singapore to acquire Nvidia chips, including founding a Chinese firm called Shanghai Century Litong. Founded in 2023, it became an Nvidia-preferred cloud partner, giving it priority access to chips, The Information reported. The Information also reported that Shanghai Century Litong facilitated buying $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia’s chips, including banned chips.

In a recent development, nvidia’s head lawyer, Tim Teter, intervened in a 2025 U.S. government probe surrounding the suspected smuggling of AI chips by Megaspeed International, Bloomberg reported. Teter contacted Commerce Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler asking questions about whether the Trump administration played a role in detaining Alice Huang.

In early 2025, Alice Huang and a business partner sought China-based investors for an Asian data center, promising they had no problem in securing GPUs, the Financial Times reported.

On Sunday night, President Trump weighed in on Huang’s controversy and showed support for the Nvidia CEO.

“I have not spoken to him about it. I just know he’s a fine person, but you never know what’s going on,” Trump mentioned.

When asked if Huang should remain chief of Nvidia, Trump mentioned, “I think so. Oh yeah, sure.”.

Jensen Huang wrote in a letter to Nvidia employees — which was also published as a press release — that he cheated on his wife.

According to recent reports, “I owe my family and all of you an apology,” Huang told his firm. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”.

Huang did not mention Alice Huang by name in the message, but linked his infidelity to “the national security concerns raised in news reports.”.

“Nvidia’s Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our firm. I am committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American,” Huang wrote.

Nvidia shares slid over 5% the following day.

Three Republican congressmen — Chairman John Moolenaar of the House Select Committee on China, Chairman Brian Mast of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, and Chairman Rick Crawford of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence — sent a request to Huang for a closed-door joint briefing with their three committees.

“Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the [People’s Republic of China]’s access to sensitive U.S. technology and information,” the chairmen wrote. “The matter of PRC infiltration and access to cutting-edge U.S. technology is core to the investigative work of our three committees this Congress. It is vital that Congress determines the extent to which U.S. national security has been placed at risk.”.

It has been revealed that U.S. officials had been investigating Alice Huang and Megaspeed for more than a year when the Newly introduced York Times broke the story in late October that the two executives also had a close relationship.

An Nvidia spokesperson denied that this relationship was something out of the ordinary.

Recent findings suggest that “Jensen’s interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected. Meetings with customers are part of a CEO’s job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year,” Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo remarked. He added that “if the U.S. government believes that any person is a threat to American industry, it would let us know.”.

Sources indicate that U.S. officials circulated a secret memo among policymakers that warned that Megaspeed’s Alice Huang, who had a relationship with Jensen Huang, was a spy for China’s Ministry of State Security. This memo was not public knowledge until it was later reported by the New York Times.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio supervised the drafting of the memo.

Around the same time, per the Fresh York Times’ report, U.S. President Donald Trump was briefed about intelligence findings that possible Chinese spy Alice Huang had formed a close relationship with Jensen Huang. Trump did not act on this information.

The Nvidia CEO, an ally of Trump, has repeatedly advocated for the U.S. government to let Nvidia expand its business in China.

Megaspeed was confirmed to be under investigation by both the U.S. and Singaporean governments in October 2025. As a customer of Nvidia, Megaspeed was suspected of helping Chinese companies get around American embargoes on chip exports.

Megaspeed, a neocloud that used Nvidia chips, had been renting computing power to Chinese internet giant Alibaba and other Chinese companies, the Times reported. A Commerce Department official who had visited Megaspeed’s data center in Malaysia in 2024 had found a hoard of Nvidia equipment that was still packed in boxes and the concern was that this equipment was being directly shipped somewhere else, like China, rather than installed and sold as a cloud service.

Jensen Huang had been spotted socializing with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang as early as 2024 in Taiwan, where the Nvidia CEO was born.

In a recent development, these investigations into Megaspeed highlighted concerns about the degree to which Nvidia is able to track its chip exports. At the time, an Nvidia spokesperson told press that the company did not have “any reason to believe products had been diverted.”.

“NVIDIA visited multiple Megaspeed sites yet again earlier this week and confirmed what we previously observed — Megaspeed is running a small commercial cloud, like many other companies throughout the world, as allowed by U.S. export control rules,” the Nvidia spokesperson stated at the time.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The historic launch is happening while Rockstar workers vote on union recognition.
  • Industry observers note that unsurprisingly, a lot of people have bought Grand Theft Auto 6.
  • According to recent reports, "It is with immense gratitude that we enter a new chapter of Rockstar Games with the release of Grand Theft Auto VI," Sam Houser, Rockstar's president and founder, stated in a statement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The historic launch is happening while Rockstar workers vote on union recognition.

Industry observers note that unsurprisingly, a lot of people have bought Grand Theft Auto 6. Rockstar Games unveiled Friday that, based on company estimates, the open-world crime game made $3.79 billion in day-one retail sales and sold 32.5 million copies in pre-release. That last total is notably above the 20 million pre-orders some analysts expected Rockstar to sell ahead of the game's launch.

According to recent reports, "It is with immense gratitude that we enter a new chapter of Rockstar Games with the release of Grand Theft Auto VI," Sam Houser, Rockstar's president and founder, stated in a statement. "We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world and we couldn't be more excited to share this moment with you.".

Recent findings suggest that GTA 6 has easily lapped the previous entry in the series, Grand Theft Auto 5, which made over $800 million worldwide from about 11 million units in its first day of sales in 2013. GTA 6 is more expensive, starting at $80 rather than GTA V's $60, but clearly demand has built up in the 13 years it took Rockstar to get the series' latest entry ready for launch.

In a recent development, after years of industry-wide layoffs, it's not clear if the game's early success will actually translate into security for Rockstar Games' workers. According to a Guardian op-ed from a Rockstar North developer, the studio's staff are worried that layoffs could happen even though the game is making money hand over fist. Rockstar workers are voting on whether they'll recognize their branch of the Independent Workers Union of Great Britain between November 12 and November 26. "We go where the team goes," Jennifer Kolbe, Rockstar's head of publishing, told Bloomberg in October. "So if they want a union, they will have a union.".

At the same time, Rockstar has been accused of union busting. The studio laid off a group of more than 30 developers in October 2025, most of whom were trying to organize its workers. Rockstar says it terminated its former employees because they were sharing confidential information, and their case has played out in an employment tribunal in the lead-up to GTA 6's release. The result of the union vote or the tribunal could shape the studio's future just as much as its latest game being a smash hit.

Uber tests rides for kids as young as 10, with extra pay for drivers

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Uber has opened its ride-hailing service to children as young as 10 in three U.S.
  • Recent findings suggest that the program, which builds on Uber’s existing teen ride-hailing service for passengers ages 13 to 17, is the latest bid by Uber to expand its customer base.
  • The Uber Kids program is stacked with mandatory requirements for parents and drivers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Uber has opened its ride-hailing service to children as young as 10 in three U.S. cities as the company tests whether there’s a market for shuttling tweens without an adult by their side. The program, called Uber Kids, released quietly over the past few weeks in Austin, Texas, Nashville, Tennessee, and Madison, Wisconsin.

Recent findings suggest that the program, which builds on Uber’s existing teen ride-hailing service for passengers ages 13 to 17, is the latest bid by Uber to expand its customer base. Uber is describing this as a limited pilot program, which means it may never expand beyond these cities or even exist by next year. But if successful, it could open up a potentially lucrative market for Uber: busy families with active kids.

The Uber Kids program is stacked with mandatory requirements for parents and drivers. Parents or guardians are the only ones who can order a ride for their child, which they can do by adding the child to their family profile and completing a mandatory onboarding that explains the built-in safety features. A parent or guardian must be present at the pickup locations for the trip to begin and also have to include a note to the driver that explains the drop off.

Meanwhile, only highly rated drivers who have been invited are allowed to participate. Those drivers are required to complete an education module that includes step-by-step instructions and must be opted into live video streaming so parents can watch the trip in real time, according to Uber.

Uber remarked it also requires PIN verification for every Uber Kids trip, and indicates all recordings will be encrypted and not available to the driver, and will use sensors and GPS data to detect if the ride goes off course, stops unexpectedly, or ends early.

Drivers who are willing to adhere to those rules to shuttle kids will get a pay bump for the effort, according to Uber. Eligible drivers will earn $7 more on every Uber Kids trip compared to a standard one, the tech giant indicates on the dedicated Uber Kids web page. Drivers will receive an extra $20 for the first Uber Kids ride they complete.

The extra compensation underscores a key challenge Uber faces as it expands into this younger age group — how to convince drivers to take on that added responsibility. If the program does expand it could eventually compete with existing transportation services such as HopSkipDrive and Zum.

It has been revealed that uber opened its ride-hailing service to minors in 2023 when it launched Uber for Teens, although the organization had conducted early pilots several years prior. As the program expanded nationwide, Uber introduced a live video streaming feature.

The news, first reported by Axios, external, follows security concerns, including the ability of advanced AI models - mostly from US companies - to discover vulnerabilities which humans would not be able to find on their own.

Earlier this week, Rubio stated there was "zero evidence" the outages were connected, adding "we are not under systemic attack".

But the fact that so many have happened in quick succession has left some people worried about the safety of the tech which is heavily relied on in all aspects of daily life.

Hacks, AI or just overdue updates - why have there been so many outages?

Cairncross was previously a lawyer in the Republican Party, before becoming the chief operating officer of the Republican National Committee.

In the first Trump administration, he was part of the team of the White House chief of staff.

#12779. Tech Report: Researcher plants 2m canaries into the AI supply chain. A privacy disaster surfaced.

📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ars Technica ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: Researcher plants 2m canaries into the AI supply chain. A privacy disaster surfaced.

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1041 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, researchers planted 2 million digital tripwires in requests sent through a sprawling network of AI services to find out what happened to sensitive information entrusted to them.
  • The exposure was found through an ingenious experiment designed to test if sensitive information can leak through the vast chain of widely used AI services and how that information is exploited when it does.
  • To test for potential leakage, researcher HD Moore assembled a collection of AWS access keys, functioning credentials tied to empty AWS accounts, passwords for services such as SSH, and unique URLs, DNS names, and private git repository references.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, researchers planted 2 million digital tripwires in requests sent through a sprawling network of AI services to find out what happened to sensitive information entrusted to them. What they discovered was an ecosystem that leaked highly sensitive data like a sieve.

The exposure was found through an ingenious experiment designed to test if sensitive information can leak through the vast chain of widely used AI services and how that information is exploited when it does. Many of today’s AI apps use services such as OpenRouter or Vercel that act as brokers. These “AI routers,” sometimes also known as “AI gateways,” receive large numbers of prompts sent from AI app end consumers and route them to an available inference engine based on criteria such as the one charging the lowest price or being best suited for the given task. Instead of using Anthropic, OpenAI, or another substantial provider, the developer hires an AI router to find the most suitable model.

To test for potential leakage, researcher HD Moore assembled a collection of AWS access keys, functioning credentials tied to empty AWS accounts, passwords for services such as SSH, and unique URLs, DNS names, and private git repository references. None of the secrets had ever been used before, and he controlled the infrastructure that received any requests using the credentials. He then seeded each secret into exactly one prompt sent to a single provider. In the event any of the secrets were leaked, these “canaries”—so called because they resemble the role of that bird when taken into coal mines—would allow Moore to identify each link in the chain that was responsible.

In a recent development, the findings are striking. They included:.

It has been revealed that “We sent nearly two million AI prompts containing unique, trackable secrets to AI providers, then watched where those secrets surfaced,” Moore, the chief research officer of security firm Dragos, wrote Thursday. “What we found revealed security breaches, prompt theft, and widespread failures to protect customer data.”.

In a recent development, although prompts are encrypted in transit, they are decrypted at each hop inside the large inference reseller network. The prompt is first sent to an AI router, which reads the plaintext in it to determine the most suitable inference providers to handle the request. Often, the prompt is then sent to a pool of available models, which sometimes run inside different hosting providers. Prompts can also pass from one AI router (such as Vercel) to another one (e.g. OpenRouter). Each one of these players is likely to log the prompt and store it for as long as its policies call for (if not indefinitely).

The most concerning of the findings was the breach of three separate hosting providers. The attackers who compromised one of the providers reused “a couple hundred” of the AWS keys. Moore wrote:.

Each key was sent in exactly one request to one provider, all within a few short windows in late October, and every request we sent during those windows was stolen. Some of the stolen keys came from requests that the provider rejected before a model ever ran—this tells us that the attacker was copying requests at the provider’s front door, and not somewhere deeper in the inference stack. In the other two breaches, some of the stolen requests were marked as ZDR. A privacy flag doesn’t help when the attacker is already inside.

Parties tied to the hack of these three providers then tested each key, in some cases within hours of being seeded, to see what kind of resources it gave access to. The parties looked through S3 buckets, secrets managers, and parameter stores in search of still more credentials. They also tried to enable hosted models in AWS Bedrock and added their own IAM customers to maintain access. In all, the stolen bait keys were used “tens of thousands” of times in AWS API calls.

It has been revealed that secrets sent to two of the hacked providers were rapidly used together, almost immediately, from the same rented server. That means the providers were almost certainly compromised by the same adversary.

It has been revealed that as noted earlier, some of the secrets were stolen by the resellers themselves. To lure prompts to their servers, they offered low prices. Then they turned on request logging, and waited. Moore identified them by sending requests to the same model through different sellers. When credentials were later reused when sent through one seller and not another, the researcher knew it was the reseller, not the model provider, that was responsible.

Last, the canary experiment revealed that some providers are scraping secret URLs put into the prompts, in violation of privacy terms. Moore wrote:.

The clearest example involves a Chinese AI lab. This lab’s systems fetched the secret URLs from more than half of the prompts that we sent to its models between July and October, including roughly two-thirds of the requests marked as “no data collection” or Zero Data Retention. The scraper typically demonstrated up two or three days after the request.

In a recent development, this wasn’t limited to requests sent to the lab directly. Several US hosting providers resell this lab’s models, and prompts sent to those providers triggered the exact same scraper—the prompts were flowing back to the lab. A customer who picked a US provider specifically to keep their data in the U.S. didn’t get what they paid for. Later on, a git client on a different cloud started trying to clone the private repositories referenced in our prompts, but only for prompts that used this lab’s models.

The researcher said he found one US hosting provider crawling a secret URL more than two months after it was used in a single inference call to its search endpoint. Another ran a scraper that came back for URLs days after each request, regardless of the AI router used to reach it.

The blockbuster research is the latest indictment exposing the lax privacy and security that’s endemic in much of the AI ecosystem. The findings mean that people who want to ensure secrets they put into prompts stay private face a daunting task that isn’t likely to become easier any time soon.

How to stream GTA 6 on your iPhone, iPad or Mac

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (828 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Because there’s no such thing as too much Vice City.
  • After an excruciatingly long wait of 13 years, Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally available to play on the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S.
  • Sources indicate that unlike cloud gaming that utilizes remote servers and often requires a subscription, remote play harnesses the power of your own console.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Because there’s no such thing as too much Vice City.

After an excruciatingly long wait of 13 years, Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally available to play on the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S. If you're taking your time to enjoy the upcoming title, it can take a while to reveal GTA 6's full map. People have taken time off work just to spend more time exploring Leonida, and if you're that excited about the game, chances are you'll want to keep playing it when you're away from your console. Well, both Sony and Microsoft offer remote play functionality on their consoles, allowing you to stream GTA 6 on your phone, tablet or computer.

Sources indicate that unlike cloud gaming that utilizes remote servers and often requires a subscription, remote play harnesses the power of your own console. It streams its video and audio feed to another device, which in this case can be an iPhone, iPad, Mac, Android phone or Windows PC. Sony offers the PS Remote Play app that you can install on your device, while Xbox lets you play remotely through the browser itself.

Sources indicate that to get started, you'll of course need either a PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X/S console with a copy of GTA 6 purchased and downloaded. Though on-screen controls may be available, a compatible gamepad, like the DualSense or Xbox controller, will make the experience considerably better, especially for a game as detailed and immersive as GTA 6.

You don't need to be connected to the same network to stream GTA 6 on your phone or computer, but a fast and stable internet connection on both ends is required to minimize input lag and connectivity complications during gameplay. Sony recommends a connection speed of 15 Mbps and Xbox suggests using a 5GHz Wi-Fi network with a speed of at least 7 – 10 Mbps.

You'll first need to configure your PS5 to work with remote play. Turn on your console, navigate to Settings > System > Remote Play and turn on the Enable Remote Play option. Head back to Settings and navigate to Power Saving > Features Available in Rest Mode. Here, turn the Stay Connected to the Internet and Enable Turning on PS5 from Network options on. These will allow you to wake your console from Rest Mode remotely so that you don't need to keep it running all the time.

Sources indicate that now, download the PS Remote Play app on your Android, iOS, macOS or Windows device. Once installed, launch the app and sign into the same PlayStation account you use on your console. Your PS5 should show up in the list of available consoles. Select it and give the app a moment to establish a remote play session with your console.

You can now interact with your PS5's interface using your phone, tablet or computer. Navigate to your game library and launch GTA 6. In our testing, the game works beautifully on both Android and iPhone with remote play on the same network. Input lag wasn't noticeable, although the DualSense controller's haptics and adaptive triggers didn't seem to kick in — these features did work on Mac and Windows with a wired connection.

It has been revealed that to connect your DualSense controller, you'll need to put it in pairing mode first. You can do this by pressing and holding both the PS and Create buttons simultaneously until the controller starts flashing blue. Head to Bluetooth settings on your device and look for DualSense Wireless Controller in the list of available devices.

If you're an Xbox user, the steps to play GTA 6 remotely on your phone or computer are very similar. First, turn your Xbox console on and navigate to Profile & system > Settings > Devices & connections > Remote features. Turn the Enable remote features toggle on and under the Power options setting, select Sleep. You have now configured your Xbox Series X/S to support remote play.

Recent findings suggest that open the browser on your smartphone, tablet or computer and head to the Xbox remote play website. Sign into your Microsoft account, select your Xbox console and tap or click on the Remote play on this device button. Once again, pairing an Xbox controller with the device you're streaming GTA 6 on will allow for much better controls. You can enter pairing mode on your Xbox controller by holding down the Pair button for three seconds. Then, head to your device's Bluetooth settings to add the controller.

Sources indicate that although Grand Theft Auto 6 is only available natively on current-gen consoles from Sony and Microsoft, Xbox One consumers can enjoy the game through Xbox Cloud Gaming. You still need to buy the game digitally and will likely spend a bit more to get additional cloud gaming hours, seeing as how the Game Pass Ultimate tier now only includes 15 hours of cloud playtime per month.

NSW passes Mount Pleasant coalmine law as Greens claim change an attempt to head off One Nation

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Labor states allowing mine to increase production reflects ‘gravity of situation facing hundreds of workers’ – but critics call it ‘unprecedented and dangerous’.
  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast.
  • The New South Wales government has passed special legislation to allow a coalmine in the Hunter Valley to increase production by 32% in its final act of parliament before the March state election, in which the region will be a key battleground for One Nation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Labor states allowing mine to increase production reflects ‘gravity of situation facing hundreds of workers’ – but critics call it ‘unprecedented and dangerous’.

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast.

The New South Wales government has passed special legislation to allow a coalmine in the Hunter Valley to increase production by 32% in its final act of parliament before the March state election, in which the region will be a key battleground for One Nation.

After a marathon session in the legislative council on Friday, the Minns government and the Coalition voted at 1.36am on Saturday morning to allow the Mount Pleasant mine to increase its annual extraction rate from 12.5MT to 16.5MT until 2032.

At the start of debate, the resources minister, Courtney Houssos, told the upper house “this is a unique bill applying to unique circumstances”.

According to recent reports, “Taking the decision to intervene in the way we have is not an easy one, but it is an vital one,” she said. “And it does reflect the gravity of the situation facing hundreds of workers and their families in the Hunter.”.

The legislation has drawn outcry from legal and anti-corruption experts, climate groups, crossbenchers and civil liberties organisations, after the high court ruled last month that an approval for an expansion that would increase the mine’s annual output to 21MT until 2048 was invalid.

In a 3-2 split ruling, the high court found the state’s Independent Planning Commission (IPC) failed to properly consider imposing conditions to minimise greenhouse gas emissions that would be generated by the mine when the coal is sold and burned overseas.

Despite saying he would not bypass the court’s decision, the NSW premier, Chris Minns, subsequently declared the legislation, claiming it would save 400 jobs ahead of Christmas.

Sources indicate that on Friday, the government and Coalition used their numbers to block almost 200 amendments to the bill sought by the Greens, who called the legislation “exceptional and unprecedented and dangerous”. Animal Justice party MLC Emma Hurst also opposed the bill.

“Labor describes the circumstances as exceptional, states this case is unique, and assures the public that other companies shouldn’t expect the same treatment,” the Greens climate spokesperson, Sue Higginson, told the parliament.

“But a political assurance offers no protection against the precedent being set.”.

She accused the premier of being motivated by a desire to withstand a threat from One Nation to Labor seats in the Hunter.

“It’s very clear to us why Chris Minns has gone here, and that is because we’re really on the eve of an election, and One Nation is right now his threat,” she stated at a press conference on Thursday.

The Hunter region, the centre of NSW’s coalmining industry, is emerging as a key battleground at the March 2027 state election. The One Nation NSW upper house candidate and former coalminer Stuart Bonds contested the Labor-held federal seat of Hunter in 2025, winning 41% of the two-candidate preferred vote. The party’s NSW leader, Mike Newman, is running in the Labor-held lower house seat of Cessnock.

Higginson told the upper house that in bringing the bill, the government had turned its back on the advice of the state’s Net Zero Commission, which has said further coalmine expansions are incompatible with meeting legislated emissions reduction targets.

Recent findings suggest that “But who seems to care any more? What does the rule of law matter when [the premier] visits the Hunter and decides he needs to do something for someone so that he can remain somewhat popular in his own mind?” she noted.

The Coalition, which supported the bill, mentioned it was “about people”.

“It’s about the hundreds of workers at MACH Energy’s Mount Pleasant mine who, since the high court handed down its decision in October, have been left wondering whether they will still have a job in the newly introduced year,” Nationals MLC Sarah Mitchell said.

She said “losing hundreds of jobs in one go would completely devastate the Hunter region”.

Industry observers note that the legislation ties consent for the mine expansion to a jobs guarantee protecting workers at the mine. Data provided to the government by the mine for the jobs guarantee, which covers more than 720 workers, is subject to an independent audit.

At a press conference on Wednesday, Minns said the legal proceedings would return to the land and environment court for consideration, but it would be “a tragedy if, in the meantime, that community effectively shut down as a result of this decision”.

“Most of the workers from Mount Pleasant live in Muswellbrook, and if the mine closed, the unemployment rate would jump by 5% just in that small town,” he said, speaking alongside workers at the mine and the Mining and Energy Union, which has welcomed the legislation.

In a report published on Tuesday, the parliament’s legislation review committee found the Mount Pleasant bill would “effectively undermine” proceedings that were still before the land and environment court and “would undermine procedural fairness” by removing avenues for legal challenge.

That report also highlighted concerns with a so-called Henry VIII clause that the barrister and anti-corruption campaigner Geoffrey Watson warned this week posed a “serious corruption risk” to the state.

The clause, allowing the resources minister of the day to override state laws as they apply to the Mount Pleasant development, was amended by the government in the lower house. Following the amendments, it cannot be used to prevent changes from being subject to Icac investigations or to change the permitted coal production limit.

The Nature Conservation Council of NSW noted the government had been “embarrassed into amending its own coalmining bill”, while the Greens said the amendments did not go far enough to constrain the power any resources minister might hold under the clause.

The Law Society of NSW remarked on Thursday it was concerned that without further amendments, the Henry VIII clause risked “undermining the rule of law”.

Houssos told the upper house on Friday the government had carefully considered concerns and moved amendments to the clause because it “recognises the importance of appropriate safeguards and accountability”.

These tech outages are giving Y2K, AI agent style

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (988 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, it’s going down, as the American rapper Yung Joc might say: the airline booking systems, banking platforms, and productivity platforms.
  • Industry observers note that apple Pay went down.
  • Recent findings suggest that the first thought, naturally, is an AI hacker invasion of some sort, especially after hackers managed to attack fridges in a grocery store and a blood bank in France a few weeks ago.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, it’s going down, as the American rapper Yung Joc might say: the airline booking systems, banking platforms, and productivity platforms. In the past two weeks, the U.S.’s top businesses have faced technical outages that have disrupted the systems that run everyday life.

Industry observers note that apple Pay went down. NASA’s internal communication network went down. The FAA had to ground all flights for hours (only the third time in history since 9/11), and Microsoft was hit with an outage that took down Outlook, Teams, and Copilot for nearly two days.

Recent findings suggest that the first thought, naturally, is an AI hacker invasion of some sort, especially after hackers managed to attack fridges in a grocery store and a blood bank in France a few weeks ago. Here in the U.S., the director of National Intelligence said these outages don’t seem related to state-sponsored terrorism, while President Trump called the complications “individual events.” Many of the companies themselves have said the outages were not caused by cyberattacks or AI attacks, but tech issues.

Only, there’s the fact that they all struck within a short timespan of each other, and just a few weeks after Cybersecurity’s so-called “Black October,” when a slew of also-unrelated cybersecurity incidents occurred on October 21, striking PHP, Node.js, LiteLLM, more.

While there’s no reason to view these outages as cyberattacks, there may be more than coincidence going on: It’s giving AI-native Y2K, frankly.

Dave DeWalt, an investor who worked in cybersecurity for more than three decades (including as president and CEO of McAfee and as vice chairman of the CISA Advisory Council for the Department of Homeland Security), also thinks it’s probably AI-related.

The technical outages are most likely the “growing pains of a security system that’s getting stronger, not weaker,” and that “AI is surfacing vulnerabilities at a speed and scale we’ve never had before through AI tools like Mythos and others,” he told TechCrunch.

The thing is, many of these technical flaws have always existed, but because AI is surfacing them so fast, enterprises are rushing to fix them before bad actors can exploit them. “That surge in patching is disrupting things in the short term,” he said.

According to recent reports, this was, perhaps, the first moment when legacy meets modern, Anusha Iyer, a software engineer and founder of the security startup Corsha, told TechCrunch. “These industrial systems were never designed to be connected, let alone securely connected in the way we are pushing them to be today,” she remarked.

Recent findings suggest that virginia Senator Mark Warner, vice chair of the Senate Intel Committee, came to a similar conclusion (although investigations are still underway as to what could be happening). “These disruptions should serve as a wake-up call. It feels like every day brings another reminder that AI is moving faster than our ability to manage its consequences,” the senator wrote on X.

Recent findings suggest that AI is reshaping how software is built, deployed, and operated, on a scale where everyone feels the sharp learning curve. Iyer cited the FAA outage as an example of legacy tech that is not as sophisticated or advanced as the technologies companies are trying to merge it with.

In less technical terms, she remarked the outage may have been caused (and preliminary findings point to this) when the FAA was trying to modernize its telecommunications infrastructure and the transition overwhelmed parts of its legacy hardware, where the new tech likely operated at a normal modern capacity while the legacy hardware couldn’t keep up.

When looked at this way, she said, AI is actually getting the bad rep. “It’s not rapid adoption of AI yet causing these outages,” she said. “The fault is the rushed mix of the legacy and modern systems without a clear understanding of operational and cyber risk or the ability to gatekeep and protect the legacy systems.”.

Organizations need a more steadfast approach to AI adoption, including more testing and prioritizing what needs to be fixed and when, DeWalt noted.

Iyer added, “These industrial systems need to be segmented more tightly and more access controlled, so as modern systems are introduced, it can be phased in and risk mitigated.”.

Actually, there might be a silver lining to all of this for companies (and for venture investors). DeWalt said he’d rather see these U.S. enterprises find and patch their flaws, even in this messy way, than have bad actors find and exploit those vulnerabilities in AI warfare that could cause even more national security issues.

According to recent reports, and maybe some aspiring founders were inspired by them. DeWalt expects a rise in companies focused on “AI-driven vulnerability management, autonomous remediation, safe patch testing and deployment, and resilience for the systems that keep critical infrastructure running,” he noted.

In a recent development, “There’s real pain in this transition as we’ve seen in the past week,” DeWalt said. “But there’s also enormous opportunity for the companies that help organizations move at AI speed without breaking things.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • How South Korea tackles cheating on its college entrance exam.
  • South Korea's education ministry says 111 candidates were found with unauthorised smart devices during a high-stakes nationwide exam, after officials introduced urgent measures to tackle rising cases of AI-assisted cheating.
  • Five of the candidates were caught red-handed using smart devices during the exam, authorities said on Friday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

How South Korea tackles cheating on its college entrance exam.

South Korea's education ministry says 111 candidates were found with unauthorised smart devices during a high-stakes nationwide exam, after officials introduced urgent measures to tackle rising cases of AI-assisted cheating.

Five of the candidates were caught red-handed using smart devices during the exam, authorities said on Friday.

Half a million students sat for the college entry exam, also known as Suneung, which took place this week under the shadow of several recent high-profile cheating scandals.

Prior to the Suneung, authorities confirmed anti-cheating measures such as emergency alerts sent to every single mobile phone in the country to detect unauthorised devices in exam halls.

On Friday, President Lee Jae Myung called for an overhaul of the exam system to tackle AI-assisted cheating.

In South Korea, public examinations "significantly affect the distribution of opportunities and resources", Lee said, adding that using AI to cheat in such tests "rocks the basic order of our society by undermining fairness and trust".

Concerns over academic dishonesty had been brewing in recent weeks, after reports of candidates cheating with the help of AI devices.

Last month, two candidates were caught cheating with AI glasses during university entrance exams.

The education ministry remarked earlier this month that four students across middle and high schools were caught using AI glasses to cheat this year.

These fears came to a boil over the weekend, when the top scorer of South Korea's certified tax accountancy exam admitted to cheating by using a miniature camera, mobile phone and AI tools.

His confession came amid speculation over his unusually high score, with just one out of 160 questions wrong.

"I used a microcamera to photograph the test questions and sent them to an AI, then checked my answers on my smartphone to commit the cheating," noted the candidate, 34-year-old Han Won-seok, in a video published on Sunday.

His confession, days ahead of the Suneung, prompted authorities to introduce last-minute measures to prevent cheating during the national exam.

The measures included nationwide emergency alerts on the exam day.

Three alerts were sent between 08:00 and 15:00 on Thursday, causing phones across the country to blare out in unison - even if they were on silent mode, and even if they belonged to tourists using data roaming.

The phones did not ring out if they were switched off or on airplane mode.

It was the first time that South Korea tapped on its national disaster alert system to catch exam cheaters.

Candidates also had to cover up the buttons on their shirts and jackets to block any hidden cameras, and authorities conducted inspections of eyewear.

All this made even honest test takers paranoid.

Ahead of the Suneung, one high school senior told the Korea Times that he was worried his horn-rimmed spectacles would be mistaken for smart glasses.

Another told news outlet Yonhap that he usually wore glasses but made an effort to put on contact lenses for the Suneung to avoid raising suspicions.

Held every November, the Suneung is an infamous eight-hour marathon of back-to-back exams.

Students attempt about 200 questions across various subjects, which include Korean, maths, English, social and natural sciences, among others.

The country itself comes to a standstill - construction work halts, planes are grounded and military training gets suspended to facilitate an optimal testing environment.

Many South Koreans see the Suneung as a culmination of years of formal education - and a turning point that determines their university placements, careers, and social statuses.

  • A upcoming draft deal omits any mention of how to phase out fossil fuels, in what campaigners call a step 'backwards' and a 'glaring regression'.
  • Like in previous years, the climate summit is likely to be extended until a consensus is reached.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Diplomats and delegates from nearly 200 countries are meeting in Antalya, Turkey.

A upcoming draft deal omits any mention of how to phase out fossil fuels, in what campaigners call a step 'backwards' and a 'glaring regression'.

Like in previous years, the climate summit is likely to be extended until a consensus is reached.

These are the major developments from the closing phase of the UN's COP31 Climate Summit in Antalya, Turkey, on Friday, November 20, 2026:.

Industry observers note that the UN climate summit in Antalya is drawing criticism from activists and campaigners who question whether global climate talks can deliver meaningful change while fossil fuel interests remain influential. Turkey and Australia, both under scrutiny for their energy policies, are leading this year's conference.

It has been revealed that activists, including Greta Thunberg, argue COP summits have become increasingly ineffective, while others defend them as a vital space to pressure governments. Climate policy experts say the talks have helped reduce projected warming, but stress that real progress depends on action taken by countries between summits, not just agreements reached at them.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In a recent development, for the Maldives, climate change is already affecting everyday life. Heavy rainfall has forced people from their homes, warmer oceans are damaging coral reefs, and changes in fish stocks are putting pressure on the country's fishing industry. Rising sea levels pose another threat to the low-lying island nation. Meanwhile, global greenhouse gas emissions continue to rise, despite more than three decades of international climate negotiations.

At COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, the Maldives' climate minister Ali Sharif discusses why progress has been so slow, what really happens during climate negotiations, and why moving away from fossil fuels is not as straightforward as it might seem.

Industry observers note that for island nations like the Maldives, switching to renewable energy comes with practical and financial challenges. So what would it take to accelerate the transition? And can the UN climate process still deliver meaningful results?

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The hosts of next year's COP, Ethiopia, found a nationally tailored sporting metaphor to sum up the difficult, ongoing, sometimes tortuous process that the global environmental meetings can prove to be.

Speaking at the end of Friday's plenary to confirm Addis Ababa's intentions to host next year's summit, Gedion Timothewos, the foreign minister and upcoming president of COP32, made reference to Ethiopia's longstanding success in endurance running in track and field.

Referring to the COP process as a marathon, not a sprint, Timothewos noted the country was looking forward to picking up the baton from Turkey and leading the next leg of the relay, taking the ongoing process forward into 2027.

His comments came during a late-night plenary session, but more talks are still expected in Antalya.

Shortly after 9 p.m. local time in Antalya, delegates gathered for a plenary session, well past the official closing time.

The Turkish presidency's opening address was partly drowned out by a protester shouting objections in English such as "you are killing the future," and gaining applause within the chamber.

Recent findings suggest that "We've been negotiating for days to find the common ground," COP31 President Murat Kurum, Turkey's environment minister, told the plenary. He hailed the progress made and said the world "waits for good news from this room.".

But the plenary session noted how several of the more ambitious aspects of a political declaration remained incomplete, with no agreement yet reached at the summit.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Several national delegates spoke during the plenary to bemoan the elusive progress or even backsliding during the two weeks of negotiations.

The evening's session, however, has been dealing with technical challenges, and the possibility that discussions continue into the weekend remains.

Attacks on climate science and disinformation risk delaying key measures at COP31 in Antalya. As the UN climate talks draw to a close, how will that affect efforts to come to an agreement?

The UN's IPCC should have already started work on its next series of multi-year scientific assessments on climate change's progress, but the process is on hold at the urging of countries including fossil fuel-producing giants Russia, Saudi Arabia and Iran.

Read Tim Schauenberg's full report on this obstruction to climate research and other similar issues complicating COP31 here.

It has been revealed that the US government is snubbing UN climate talks in Turkey. That's prompted a delegation of American lawmakers, mayors and governors to make the trip instead, aiming to show that climate action in the US is alive and well.

Head over to this report to learn more about who is representing the US at the summit, even if President Donald Trump, who has repeatedly dismissed global warming as a "hoax", didn't send a formal delegation for the second year in a row.

It has been revealed that funding from wealthy countries to help deal with the impacts of climate change hasn't materialized, indicates Uganda's environment minister. The East African country is hoping oil and carbon credits will help boost finances.

Learn more about what Uganda's environment minister Beatrice Atim Anywar stated about climate financing in this report.

Veteran climate justice advocate Victor Menotti of the Demand Climate Justice NGO told DW that European governments appeared to be copying US President Donald Trump's negotiating playbook at COP this year.

"We know the US isn't here, but we can see that Germany and other European governments have learned a few of the Trump tactics, maybe in the trade disputes with the US," Menotti said. "And we see them applying here in Antalya, where it's like: Don't admit to anything. Try to dilute your responsibilities. Weaken whatever obligations you have. And then take even more.".

He argued these countries were also expecting unreasonable or unfeasible commitments from developing countries, for instance restrictions on what they can spend money on and obligations to report on their expenditures.

"Germany is subsidizing quite a bit of coal still and fossil fuels, LNG expansion infrastructure," he remarked, arguing that wealthier countries' energy spending also had room for improvement.

"We need the North to act first," Menotti noted. "The deal from Paris, the deal from Rio 30 years ago, is that the North will lead. But yet we see too much bullying of the global South and not enough leadership like they agreed to.".

You can cross off another box on your COP31 bingo cards, dear readers.

Industry observers note that as of the top of this hour, the session has officially gone past its scheduled end time of 1500 GMT/UTC on Friday, or 6 p.m. local time on site in Turkey.

According to recent reports, this is something of an annual tradition at COP summits, which are always scheduled to finish at the end of a working week but also almost invariably run into the closing weekend. Delegates and members of the media tend to book their travel plans with this in mind.

The revised draft declaration, which critics have slammed as "watered down" due to the omission of fossil fuels, highlights the "electrification" of the global economy as a central pillar of the energy transition.

"Electrification is the key to transitioning away from fossil fuels," Australian Climate Minister Chris Bowen told reporters.

What are the key points to know about the "35-by-35" electrification target?

But the text does not specify what energy sources would supply the electricity. Some countries are demanding that the text call for "clean" electrification to clearly favor renewable sources over coal, oil or gas.

Bowen, who has been trying to secure compromises, pledged to continue working over the "coming hours, for as long as it takes, to get the job done.".

In a recent development, "People have strong views of course — I am not stepping away from that. But no one has noted to me let's give up and go home," Bowen said.

The Climate Action Network (CAN), a global network of over 2,500 civil society organizations, has accused wealthy developed nations, led by the EU, "of blocking every track" towards a substantive agreement on fighting climate change and curbing fossil fuel use.

At its final press conference of the summit, CAN executive director Tasneem Essop noted the group was "rejecting what is currently on the table.".

Industry observers note that "There is nothing (...) that protects people or addresses the priorities of the Global South. In fact, the opposite is true. The current text has opened the door to the most harmful and dangerous options of any COP so far," Essop said.

She pointed out that this year's COP had the highest ever number of lobbyists for fossil fuels, for AI, for CCUS (Carbon Capture, Utilization, and Storage) and for CDR (Carbon Dioxide Removal), which only represent corporate interests and do not have the interests of the people from developing nations who are most at risk from global warming in mind.

"What we’re leaving this COP with is decisions made to promote the interests of those corporations making profits from the destruction of people," Essop mentioned.

In a recent development, mohamed Adow from Power Shift Africa, which is also part of CAN, noted: "The COP Presidents want to tell us this has been a great COP. Well, I can tell you without any doubt that this has been the worst COP ever.

"Overseeing a failing COP is bad enough, but trying to sell it as a success rubs salt into the wounds of those people who need it to deliver.".

Adow cautioned that communities that live with the constant threat of drought, floods and failed harvests were "promised action.".

"They cannot survive on an annual renewal of promises," Adow said.

Sources indicate that he laid the blame squarely with the world's most developed nations: "They demand action from developing countries, then block public finance, block Just Transition, block climate finance, and they expect ambition. You cannot keep your foot on the brake and complain that countries are not moving fast enough.".

Xiye Bastida, a New York-based youth activist from Mexico, spoke to DW's Katharina Schantz to describe her frustration over the lack of progress and ambition on display at this year's COP Summit, which is the seventh the 24-year-old has attended.

Bastida, who has played a leading role in the Fridays for Future climate movement in Fresh York, stated she did not think she "could be more disappointed" at how climate targets are "being rolled back.".

"This is really the time of reckoning," Bastida mentioned.

Sources indicate that she explained that she had changed her flight plans to be able to stay until the end, because she feels "we have to be here. We at least to be witnesses of how they're taking things away.".

Bastida pointed to the hypocrisy from wealthy nations, who have blamed some from the Global South for not wanting the summit's joint declaration to mention fossil fuels.

"But they (the Global North) are the ones not bringing the money, and they're the ones who are not bringing the ambition.

Industry observers note that "And they want to show themselves as the leaders. But if you want to mention fossil fuels so bad, where's the money for the transition? Where are the roadmaps?

"Are you serious?" Bastida concluded.

The new draft declaration, which, as we've reported, has been panned by the EU and civil society, has also disappointed some of the world's least developed countries (LDCs) that are most vulnerable to climate change.

The LDC Group, which comprises 44 of the world's least wealthy nations, came into this year's COP summit hoping for stronger climate action than what has been achieved so far.

"It’s a moment of anticipation," Lamin Sheriff, a press attache for the Sierra Leone government, told DW's Katharina Schantz.

In a recent development, "Ministers from LDCs have requests on the table for the presidency. So whilst they wait on what the outcome would be, everybody is waiting patiently. So the moment is really: we are hopeful for the future, but we are also worried because if proper care is not taken, all what we have debated about here in the last couple of weeks will just be a talk show (…) We can't do anything at the moment.".

From clashes over fossil fuels to disputes over climate finance, COP31 exposes the contradictions at the heart of global climate diplomacy.

Climate activist Greta Thunberg indicates that COP has turned into a "greenwashed circus.".

But supporters say the world would be worse off without the COP process.

DW's Tim Schauenberg reports from the summit in Antalya.

Here's the latest dispatch from DW's Tim Schauenberg, who is in Antalya covering the COP31 summit for us:.

"Formally speaking, the final hours of the climate conference have begun. The countries' pavilions have been coming down since Thursday: empty halls, chopped-up timber, lonely lecterns.

It has been revealed that things don't look quite so bleak yet at the negotiations in Antalya, Turkey, and yet, time is running out here. If this is indeed to be, as the COP31 President has already declared, the "best COP ever," the delegations here will have to step up their efforts considerably.

At present, the corridors are buzzing with discussions amongst scientists, NGOs and media representatives. The delegations are doing what they are here to do: negotiating. So, the long wait has begun — not just for a final decision, but also for substance.

Because that is what has been lacking here in Antalya.

In a recent development, under discussion is a global target to generate 35% of primary energy from electricity by 2035. The EU is determined that this electricity should be generated from solar and wind power. Other countries, particularly those reliant on fossil fuels, want to block the target altogether.

Positions have hardened on this issue — and others — even after two weeks of negotiations. An EU spokesperson is currently making her way through the media center; anyone who doesn't bump into her in the corridors will receive a phone call. The message: the EU will not accept the latest draft of the negotiations as it stands.

According to recent reports, this is partly because the issue of carbon capture and storage features prominently in the presidency's latest summary of the negotiations. However, this is expensive and technically complex, and will not halt the climate crisis. Nor is there presently any consensus on turning our backs on the root cause — namely, the burning of coal, oil and gas.

The likelihood that an agreement on this last point will be reached is close to zero, since all 197 countries must agree to this, and Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iran and India have no interest in fundamentally questioning their revenue streams and energy plans in the near future.

In a recent development, so the coffee stands are well stocked, and everyone is keeping at least one eye on the flickering screens in the long halls that display all the events on today's agenda. So far, there is a gaping void when it comes to the sessions intended for the press. That could change at any moment — or take hours.

Recent findings suggest that quite a few media representatives have already brought bags full of provisions with them this morning. They are clearly preparing for a long weekend.".

They asked founder Brewster Kahle to voluntarily recognize the union, but will go to an NLRB vote if needed.

In a recent development, workers at the Internet Archive, home to the Wayback Machine, are unionizing. After signing up to join the Communications Workers of America (CWA), they're asking founder Brewster Kahle to voluntarily recognize the union. As a backup, they've filed for a National Labor Relations Board (NLRB) election. Kahle hasn't responded publicly yet.

Sources indicate that wired reports that over 80 of 124 eligible US workers signed on. None of their asks are radical: better pay, additional benefits that apply to everyone and paths for career development and promotion. Organizing committee member Danielle Leard tied the unionization campaign to the Internet Archive's mission, stating that job security, benefits and livable wages go "hand-in-hand with sustaining the Archive long-term.".

There's a recent precedent from another Bay Area nonprofit. Wikimedia Foundation workers joined the CWA in September, but only after the foundation refused to voluntarily recognize the effort and it went to an NLRB vote. Wikimedia workers ultimately voted in favor by a count of 158 to 14.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Meta plans to charge $300 for Muse Charm, its upcoming Tamagotchi-like AI device that was teased at the tech giant’s Connect event earlier this year, The Information has reported.

When reached for comment by TechCrunch, a Meta spokesperson didn’t deny the claims, merely providing the following statement: “We’re charmed by the interest in our AI devices, and we’ll have more to share soon.”.

So far, Meta has made a relatively successful push into consumer AI, launching Muse — its agentic helper — along with a variety of cute avatars that people can use to give the system more of a personality.

Muse Charm, the organization’s push into AI hardware, will allow owners to carry a physical personification of its software around in their pocket (or potentially wear it around their neck), talking to it, asking it questions, and giving it commands.

It remains to be seen whether customers will bite or not. AI wearables have had a rough go of it so far (here’s looking at you, Humane Ai pin), but companies continue to iterate on the concept in an attempt to break through to a broader audience.

In a recent development, indeed, $300 is arguably a pretty steep price for a product the size of a keychain, although it’s also a price point that’s in line with what other companies have been charging. The wearable launched by Friend — the AI startup whose device lets you text and talk to an AI persona — is currently retailing for $250. On the other hand, Amazon’s all-newly introduced Bee Frontier wearable AI device — which transcribes conversations and tracks tasks — lists for $75 and is currently on a Black Friday, 30% off sale of $52.49. Even with its $99/year subscription to let it tie into a user’s apps (photos, emails, etc.), it’s still far less expensive than Muse Charm.

Meta reconsiders 2030 net-zero goal amid record emissions from AI data centers

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (688 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, meta’s executives are rethinking the organization’s original goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2030.
  • The organization’s 2026 sustainability report claims that “our long-term ambitions haven’t changed, but our operating environment has,” according to an introduction from Rachel Peterson, vice president of data centers at Meta, and Blair Swedeen, global head of net zero and sustainability at Meta.
  • “We are re-evaluating our timelines, sequencing, and interim milestones—including the 2030 timeframe for our net zero emissions goal and our near-term intensity targets—so our approach reflects current operating realities while keeping progress transparent year over year,” Peterson and Swedeen wrote in the report.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, meta’s executives are rethinking the organization’s original goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2030. That revelation in Meta’s latest sustainability report comes as the company reported a record percentage increase in greenhouse gas emissions that exceeds any other Big Tech competitor racing to build fresh AI data centers.

The organization’s 2026 sustainability report claims that “our long-term ambitions haven’t changed, but our operating environment has,” according to an introduction from Rachel Peterson, vice president of data centers at Meta, and Blair Swedeen, global head of net zero and sustainability at Meta. In the November 19, 2026, report, they attributed the changing conditions and the need for a rethink to how “demand for AI infrastructure has grown faster than almost anyone projected.”.

“We are re-evaluating our timelines, sequencing, and interim milestones—including the 2030 timeframe for our net zero emissions goal and our near-term intensity targets—so our approach reflects current operating realities while keeping progress transparent year over year,” Peterson and Swedeen wrote in the report.

Meta’s statement about re-evaluating its 2030 emissions goal is a significant public acknowledgment, given that Amazon, Google, and Microsoft have all stuck by their original sustainability goals so far.

But all the companies have acknowledged challenges in balancing their original sustainability goals against the breakneck buildout of hyperscale data centers. Despite efforts to invest in more renewable energy projects, Meta and its rivals are still often pushing forward on AI data centers that rely on burning natural gas to generate electricity.

Meta’s report described the tech giant’s total emissions as surging from 15.6 million metric tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent in 2024 to more than 21.7 million metric tonnes in 2025.

That would make Meta’s annual carbon footprint roughly comparable to total emissions for the state of Idaho, while surpassing the total emissions of states such as Hawaii, Maine, South Dakota, and New Hampshire. The firm attributed much of this emissions increase to “capital goods,” like as data center servers.

That also represents a nearly 40 percent increase in Meta’s carbon footprint between 2024 and 2025, which is the highest percentage year-over-year increase for total emissions reported by any of the four major US tech giants.

For comparison, Microsoft reported a 25 percent increase in its overall carbon footprint, Google reported an 18 percent increase, and Amazon’s report described a 16 percent increase between 2024 and 2025. However, Meta still likely has one of the smallest total carbon footprints among the Big Tech companies.

Meta’s approach to achieving net-zero emissions has included developing fresh renewable energy projects to match emissions and using carbon removal technology.

But even when factoring in such efforts, Meta still reported net emissions increasing from more than 8.1 million metric tonnes to more than 11.8 million metric tonnes for 2025. That represents a 45 percent increase.

From a water consumption standpoint, Meta reported progress in reducing facility consumption from 825 million gallons in 2024 to 790 million gallons in 2025.

Yet that positive trend is tempered by the fact that Meta also described an increase in water consumption from “areas with water stress,” rising from 198 million gallons in 2024 to 246 million gallons in 2025.

It has been revealed that meta also reported a sharp increase in water consumption related to purchased electricity—the amount of water consumed by related power generation—from 19 billion gallons in 2024 to more than 26 billion gallons in 2025. This once again highlights that, for data centers, the far bigger water usage comes from the power plants that supply electricity to data centers as opposed to data centers directly using water for cooling.

Still, some minor credit is due. The publication Data Center Dynamics pointed out that “Meta is the only hyperscaler to report indirect water use, a growing concern as data centers shift to closed-loop cooling systems that, despite using less water at source, require more electricity to run.”.

It would very much be in the public interest for other Massive Tech companies to follow suit on the reporting front—and public pressure continues to build after the AI backlash impact on US midterm election results.

During an interview with Elle Spain, Carys Douglas said her parents "do not hide" from her that people would have preconceived ideas about her.

Catherine Zeta Jones has declared the phrase "nepo baby" is "horrific".

The couple's children, Dylan and Carys, have both followed in their footsteps into acting.

Michael Douglas stated his children have been performing "since they were in kindergarten".

Recent findings suggest that "Every play, every show, summer theater camps, graduating... I mean, they've done so much work. It's unbelievable," he said.

Carys Douglas described Three Cliffs Bay in Gower Peninsula, Swansea, as "stunning".

US president appeared to doze off while Chinese leader made speech, but White House insisted he was awake.

Donald Trump was, again, accused of falling asleep during a televised event, this time during the speech of the Chinese president, Xi Jinping, at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit in China.

The US president appeared to close his eyes for roughly 10 seconds on Thursday. As his eyes closed, Trump’s head tilted downward, and his hands remained clasped in front of him.

Several prominent Trump critics on social media alleged that the US president was asleep, including Republicans Against Trump, California governor Gavin Newsom’s press office and conservative lawyer George Conway.

White House officials denied the allegations, claiming the 80-year-old US president was looking down at papers in front of him.

“Fake News! President Trump was looking at papers in front of him while the speaker made remarks. You can clearly see his eyes move back and forth,” Steven Cheung, the White House director of communications, wrote on X in response to a Newsweek article.

“This is why the people despise media so much. They constantly lie,” Cheung added.

Trump often faces accusations of falling asleep during televised events such as Oval Office press conferences, cabinet meetings and sporting events.

Occasionally, while listening to other people speak, the US president will close his eyes for several seconds, appearing as though he is falling asleep. Despite footage of the instances going viral, the White House and Trump allies have insisted the US president does not fall asleep during meetings.

In a recent development, administration officials have excused Trump’s apparent drowsiness as blinking or an example of the president listening intently. They consistently claim Trump “doesn’t sleep”.

Marco Rubio, the US secretary of state, testified to lawmakers earlier this year that he had “never seen” Trump fall asleep.

“On the contrary, the guy doesn’t sleep, which is a major problem because he calls me at two in the morning,” Rubio said in June.

Last year, JD Vance noted that Trump hardly ever sleeps, even while traveling overnight.

Recent findings suggest that “If we go on a 20-hour trip somewhere, he doesn’t sleep the entire time. And of course, if he’s not sleeping, if he’s working, he expects everybody else to be working too,” Vance told Fox News.

It has been revealed that trump became the oldest US president ever inaugurated when he was sworn in nearly two years ago. Despite his age, Trump often claims he is in near-perfect health, often bragging about his “perfect” cognitive test results and insisting he has a lot of energy.
